subject: physics_2
question_text: The horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field at a certain place is 2.6×10⁻⁵ T and the angle of dip is 60°. What is the magnetic field of the earth at this location?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: H = B cos θ, so B = H / cos 60° = 2.6×10⁻⁵ / (1/2) = 5.2×10⁻⁵ T, matching the book's worked value.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Relation and substitution
steps.mark_note: B = H / cos θ with values in
lines: The horizontal component of the earth's
field is H = B cos θ, so
steps.margin_note: First mark. Start from H = B cos θ — the dip θ is the angle the total field B makes with the horizontal.
steps.why: The total field B leans at the dip angle θ below the horizontal, so its horizontal part is B cos θ. That equals the given H, and dividing by cos θ recovers B.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by cos θ instead of dividing. H is the component, so H = B cos θ and B = H / cos θ.
Using sin 60°. The vertical component carries sin θ; the horizontal one carries cos θ.

recall.must_convey: That the horizontal component is B cos θ, so the total field is H divided by cos 60°.
reject: five point two into ten power minus five

steps.memory_tip: The component is smaller than the whole: H = B cos θ, so to get B back, divide by cos θ.

steps.label: The result
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing by 1/2 doubles the number: 2.6 becomes 5.2.
steps.why: cos 60° = 1/2, so B is exactly twice H. The unit stays tesla because only a pure number divided H.
common_mistakes: Writing 1.3×10⁻⁵ T — that comes from multiplying by 1/2 instead of dividing.
Dropping the power of ten or the unit T in the final line.

recall.must_convey: That the earth's total field there is 5.2 × 10⁻⁵ tesla, twice the horizontal component.
accept: five point two into ten power minus five tesla

steps.memory_tip: At 60° dip the total field is double the horizontal component, because cos 60° = 1/2.

insider_note: The whole numerical depends on one choice — divide by cos 60°, not multiply — and the halved answer 1.3×10⁻⁵ is the mistake the examiner sees most.
